questions.q: Discuss the significance of the Ajanta murals in the Indian painting tradition.
answer: The murals of the Ajanta caves in Maharashtra are the finest surviving ancient paintings of India and a milestone in its art.

answer.text: Painted on the walls and ceilings of these Buddhist rock-cut caves, the murals depict the life of the Buddha and the Jataka stories of his previous births. Among the most famous figures are the Bodhisattvas Padmapani and Vajrapani, shown with serene grace.

The paintings were done in the tempera technique, using natural colours on a prepared plaster ground. The artists achieved soft shading, volume and lifelike expression, so that the figures seem full of emotion and movement.
Recognised as a World Heritage Site, Ajanta set the standard for later Indian mural painting and influenced art across Asia.

answer: Thus Ajanta remains the crowning achievement of early Indian painting.
